chapter: Buck's Legion band and later gigs
title: Lakefront July Fourth job interrupted by a fight
summary: Playing before a brawl on the lakefront; interviewer mentions 'dancing with tears in my eyes'.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: That was in, I think it was in the Coventon. It was on the 4th of July. And we had a spot job. It was on the lakefront right out there. I don't quite remember the name of the place. But before a big fight started, so the sheriffs had troops of Teague, the ass around Aunt Florida. Everybody out there was dancing with tears in our eyes. You know that when Hank... You had to quit a while. You had to quit for about an hour. Yeah. Until it all settled down. Yeah.

You know, uh, you know Hank Kamen? What's that? Hank Kamen, he's a clarinet and saxophone player. He's from the way. No. He played on the president every Saturday night, so... When he sings... When he sings... Did he get over?

Oh, they have an invitation to you. Yeah, you know, you can't get over that. No, but... He, uh... He sings, I'm dancing with tears in my eyes because a girl in my arms is a boy. And nobody on the boat notices except a few old divers, you know. They don't ever catch it, you know. People don't ever listen to what's going on. They're too busy dancing on the boat.
They're trying to spook each other or something. Yeah. Did, uh...
